analysis.title: Inflation and Riksbank minutes
key_insights: Equity markets rebounded sharply on 9 November after the prior week's declines. The Nasdaq rose 2.7%, led by tech, even though Nvidia fell while its CEO Jensen Huang is under FBI investigation.
Asian equities continued higher on 10 November, with the Nikkei up 3% and the Kospi up over 4%. Stock futures point to a positive open in Europe and the US.

Oil fell further on 9 November and continued lower on 10 November after Trump said the war with Iran is "effectively over" militarily. The dollar weakened broadly and the Swedish krona strengthened against most currencies.
SEB's New Nordic Outlook says growth is challenged by rising interest rates and high energy prices, but global GDP is still growing by just over 3% this year.

SEB expects US core CPI to rise 0.25% m/m in October, slightly above the trend earlier this year. It sees signs of indirect effects from high energy prices and clearer price pressure in IT and electronic goods.

Headline US CPI probably also rose in October, but recent declines in crude oil and petrol prices point to slower inflation ahead. No y/y rates are published for the October CPI because of last year's government shutdown.

SEB expects Norwegian core inflation (CPI-ATE) to have fallen 0.2ppt to 2.8% y/y in October, a tenth above Norges Bank's forecast. Goods price increases are likely to slow in 2027 given NOK appreciation this year, while high wage costs keep service inflation elevated through next year.
Norwegian households are under pressure from high interest rates and cost pressures, and consumer confidence fell again in Q4.
Swedish PM Ulf Kristersson's report to the parliament Speaker on government formation talks was postponed to the end of the week.

SEB expects Swedish business-sector production to have slowed in September after five months of rising output. Growth is broad-based and strongest in industry. Teknikföretagen forecasts strong industrial growth this year and next and is optimistic on hiring.

All Riksbank Executive Board members supported last week's policy rate hike. The press release said a further rise is "likely" in the coming year in line with the September forecast. SEB calls this vague and open to a cautious approach, while Governor Thedéen sounded more hawkish at the press conference.

SEB believes the Riksbank minutes will show divergent views on the timing of the next hike. It expects Göran Hjelm to indicate higher downside risks to the rate path and Anna Seim to argue for more hikes.

macro_indicators.interpretation: SEB's estimate is slightly above the trend earlier this year, with some indirect energy effects and rising IT and electronics goods prices.
Falling crude and petrol prices indicate slower inflation ahead.
A fall of 0.2ppt from September and a tenth above Norges Bank's forecast, with services inflation expected to stay elevated through 2027.
Growth continues despite higher interest rates and energy prices.

macro_indicators.reading: Raised last week, further hikes likely in the coming year
macro_indicators.interpretation: The decision was unanimous. The press release language was vague, while the Governor's press conference tone was more hawkish.

risk_factors: High energy prices and rising interest rates challenge global growth.
Indirect effects of energy prices and rising IT and electronics goods prices could keep US core inflation firmer.
High wage costs could keep Norwegian service inflation elevated through 2027.
Divergent views among Riksbank members on the timing of the next hike.
geopolitical: Trump said the war with Iran is "effectively over" militarily, and oil fell as a result.
Negotiations on the war in Ukraine begin on 10 November in Abu Dhabi.
Swedish government formation talks are ongoing, and the PM's report to the Speaker was postponed to the end of the week.
